newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr/yen seen at 105 in year's time - Goldman Sachs.
newsitem.headline: Dlr/yen seen at 105 in year's time - Goldman Sachs.

text.p: The yen is expected to strengthen to 105 to the dollar by next year, a Goldman Sachs economist told a seminar on Tuesday.

Gavyn Davies, chief international economist at Goldman Sachs International London, said that while the yen is now below the "equilibrium" rate of 110 to the dollar, it is expected to strengthen over the coming year towards 105.
"The yen will strengthen to 105 yen by the time we meet next year," he said.
The yen was standing at around 122 to the dollar in late Tokyo trade.
He expects a widening trade surplus with the United States and better-than-expected economic growth in Japan to improve the Japanese currency's prospects.
He forecast real gross domestic product (GDP) growth of 1.7 percent for Japan in 1997 and 2.9 percent growth for 1998.

Tetsufumi Yamakawa, vice president and director of Goldman Sachs (Japan) Ltd's Japan Economic Research section, also told the seminar that the yen would appreciate and gave an average yen/dollar rate of 108 in the 1997/98 business year against an estimated rate of 112 in 1996/97.
He also forecast an average dollar/mark rate of 1.53 in 1997/98 against a projected rate of 1.55 in 1996/97.
